# Read-Back

A technician is streaking three overnight cultures onto selective agar plates to isolate single colonies, then reading the growth characteristics and performing a purity check with Gram staining. The work involves one technician and one supervisor who must sign off on the plate readings before subculturing. The key bottleneck is a 37 °C incubator with only one shelf that holds two plates: plates 1 and 2 go in overnight (16–20 hours), while plate 3 must wait on the bench and incubate for 6 hours once space frees up. The entire process includes setup (cleaning, labeling), streaking all three cultures at the burner's single loop station, overnight incubation of the first two, reading all three plates, then picking colonies into broth, streaking a purity plate (which must wait for supervisor approval), incubating that plate for 8 hours, and finally Gram staining and microscopy. No finish-by deadline is given; the work should complete as soon as the biology allows. The text is complete and contains no missing sections.
